items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had a quartet. Mike Longwell and Paul -- Paul -­ [indiscernible], but Paul West [phonetic sp.].

ctx.x: And now -- now what are you doing?

Well, I left Vegas and I -- I had a quartet. Mike Longwell and Paul -- Paul -­ [indiscernible], but Paul West [phonetic sp.]. And -- and the drummer. Oh, I forgot what the drummer's name was. But anyway, we did some clubs and things and then I -- I kept doing that. Then finally, I moved -- I moved to Canada. Okay? And I lived in Canada for about 3 -- 3 years.
When did you -- when did you leave New York City and go to Canada?

items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Moody and I. Moody was staying here and we went over to see him.

ctx.x: Thanks for sharing all that. That was great. You were with Dizzy when he passed away?

Yeah. I was there the night before, that was the last time he was conscious. Moody and I. Moody was staying here and we went over to see him. He had tubes and all — and I walked the room and Dizzy looked at us and went [gestures] and he blew his cheeks out. He grabbed my hand and he was doing like this. So I said, “Man, aren’t you taking this a little too far?” And he started laughing. And he couldn’t talk but he was just — and so he went into a coma and the next day he died. But he was in a coma when he died. He…
know who was in the room. But the last time he was conscious was the night before. The last people he saw before he went into the coma was Dizzy — I mean James Moody and myself.
